Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") BY NAME in the packet: an approval comment, owner note or email saying this specific item was not commissioned, not requested, not authorised, or is excluded ("approved except for X", "we did not order the Y"); rejecting a named line because it was never authorised declines it, and so does an approval that accepts the invoice except this named line, whatever reason it gives. A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AGR-2026-47.") BY NAME in the packet: an approval comment, owner note or email saying this specific item was not commissioned, not requested, not authorised, or is excluded ("approved except for X", "we did not order the Y"); rejecting a named line because it was never authorised declines it, and so does an approval that accepts the invoice except this named line, whatever reason it gives. A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

question: Invoice line 2 ("Remote Diagnostics & Fault Triage (retainer coverage) — monitoring and triage actions logged for 28 Jun–27 Jul 2026; escalation guidance provided within agreed response windows. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AGR-2026-47.") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

   "text": "Monthly Service Note — Managed Equipment Support Services, Climate Resilience Program\nService period: 2026-06-28 to 2026-07-27\nClient: Banksia Harbour Grants Foundation Ltd\nAgreement ref: AGR-2026-47\n\nD1 – Preventive Maintenance Schedule & Coordination\n- Rolling PM calendar issued 2026-06-30 covering all 14 active grantee sites.\n- Confirmed upcoming service windows with site contacts at Gladstone, Mackay, Bundaberg, Hervey Bay, Townsville (North), Townsville (South), Cairns, Rockhampton, Emerald, Longreach, Ipswich, Logan, Redlands, and Gold Coast.\n- Dispatch/return tracking updated in shared portal for scheduled sensor swap-outs at Mackay (2026-07-08) and Bundaberg (2026-07-15). question: The project owner or approver has declined invoice line 3 ("Calibration Tracking Register maintenance (retainer coverage) — register refresh and expiry alerts issued for instruments due in July/Aug 2026; recertification scheduling coordination. Period 28 Jun–27 Jul 2026. Ref: ...") BY NAME in the packet: an approval comment, owner note or email saying this specific item was not commissioned, not requested, not authorised, or is excluded ("approved except for X", "we did not order the Y"); rejecting a named line because it was never authorised declines it, and so does an approval that accepts the invoice except this named line, whatever reason it gives. A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

question: Invoice line 3 ("Calibration Tracking Register maintenance (retainer coverage) — register refresh and expiry alerts issued for instruments due in July/Aug 2026; recertification scheduling coordination. Period 28 Jun–27 Jul 2026. Ref: ...") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

Answer NO for a recurring service billing a NEW period (a later month, a later application number) however alike the prior invoices look, for a genuinely later phase or shipment, for a re-bill of a prior invoice that was reversed or credited, and when no prior invoice covers this work. Period 28 Jun–27 Jul 2026. Ref: PO-BHGF...") BY NAME in the packet: an approval comment, owner note or email saying this specific item was not commissioned, not requested, not authorised, or is excluded ("approved except for X", "we did not order the Y"); rejecting a named line because it was never authorised declines it, and so does an approval that accepts the invoice except this named line, whatever reason it gives. A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

question: Invoice line 4 ("Spare Parts Logistics & Procurement Advisory (retainer coverage) — lead-time and customs documentation guidance for replacement consumables; coordination notes for active cases. Period 28 Jun–27 Jul 2026. Ref: PO-BHGF...") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

question: The project owner or approver has declined invoice line 5 ("On-Call Technical Advisory (retainer coverage) — ad hoc support to program/grantee field technicians (calls/video sessions) during 28 Jun–27 Jul 2026. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AGR-2026-47.") BY NAME in the packet: an approval comment, owner note or email saying this specific item was not commissioned, not requested, not authorised, or is excluded ("approved except for X", "we did not order the Y"); rejecting a named line because it was never authorised declines it, and so does an approval that accepts the invoice except this named line, whatever reason it gives. A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AGR-2026-47.") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

question: At least one substantive line of this invoice is described so generically that its own text does not say what was bought, for which period, or under which authorization: "Professional services", "Consulting services", "Services rendered", "Work performed", "Project work per agreement", "Professional fees". Judge the line text itself, not what the PO or contract would let you guess. A line that names a deliverable, item, part or work code is specific even if brief; a period, quantity or rate alone does not rescue a line that never says what was bought. A code or abbreviation that any document in the packet decodes is specific; one nothing in the packet decodes is vague; a work-order, ticket or project code counts as specific only where the packet ties it to a described item, service or deliverable. Naming only the project or engagement the work relates to does not cure a line that never says what was bought. Tax, freight and expense lines do not count.

Tax charged once at one rate, or a legitimately mixed-rate supply the lines explain, is NO. Do not judge whether tax is charged twice at the same rate; code compares the amounts. A rate is read only from a percentage the line or summary states; a tax line stating no rate does not by itself establish two rates.

An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

question: Invoice line 1 ("Services - July 2026") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

question: Invoice line 2 ("Services rendered") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

question: Invoice line 3 ("Professional fees") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

question: Invoice line 4 ("Services rendered") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

Normal notices never count: '60 days overdue, service suspends per contract', polite chasers, 'please prioritise', a reminder that a due date has passed. A vendor's claim that its own bank account is frozen, blocked or under review, offered with new payment details and a short deadline, IS the pattern.

question: At least one substantive line of this invoice is described so generically that its own text does not say what was bought, for which period, or under which authorization: "Professional services", "Consulting services", "Services rendered", "Work performed", "Project work per agreement", "Professional fees". Judge the line text itself, not what the PO or contract would let you guess. A line that names a deliverable, item, part or work code is specific even if brief; a period, quantity or rate alone does not rescue a line that never says what was bought. A code or abbreviation that any document in the packet decodes is specific; one nothing in the packet decodes is vague; a work-order, ticket or project code counts as specific only where the packet ties it to a described item, service or deliverable. Naming only the project or engagement the work relates to does not cure a line that never says what was bought. Tax, freight and expense lines do not count.

question: Invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

question: Invoice line 2 ("Manual Test-Units — Remediation-Validation Re-Tests (critical findings from June API assessment, SEC-2026-0133)") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

question: Invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

question: Invoice line 4 ("Secure Media Handling & Courier — Encrypted USB delivery of raw scan artefacts to BHGF Harbour St office") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

Normal notices never count: '60 days overdue, service suspends per contract', polite chasers, 'please prioritise', a reminder that a due date has passed. A vendor's claim that its own bank account is frozen, blocked or under review, offered with new payment details and a short deadline, IS the pattern.

question: At least one substantive line of this invoice is described so generically that its own text does not say what was bought, for which period, or under which authorization: "Professional services", "Consulting services", "Services rendered", "Work performed", "Project work per agreement", "Professional fees". Judge the line text itself, not what the PO or contract would let you guess. A line that names a deliverable, item, part or work code is specific even if brief; a period, quantity or rate alone does not rescue a line that never says what was bought. A code or abbreviation that any document in the packet decodes is specific; one nothing in the packet decodes is vague; a work-order, ticket or project code counts as specific only where the packet ties it to a described item, service or deliverable. Naming only the project or engagement the work relates to does not cure a line that never says what was bought. Tax, freight and expense lines do not count.

Wording, amount or invoice number may differ. Answer NO for a recurring service billing a NEW period (a later month, a later application number) however alike the prior invoices look, for a genuinely later phase or shipment, for a re-bill of a prior invoice that was reversed or credited, and when no prior invoice covers this work. Answer NO where the prior invoice bills this invoice's obligation AS A WHOLE (the same milestone, application, shipment or period that the whole invoice bills, or a re-issue of the same invoice): that is the prior-relation question, not a re-billed line; re-billed is for one old line slipped into an otherwise new invoice. YES for a catch-up or cumulative-adjustment charge for earlier months whose retainer a paid prior invoice already billed. If you cannot point to the specific prior invoice that already billed it, answer NO.

question: Invoice line 1 ("VF-M3-PH2-GWPKG") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

question: Invoice line 2 ("VF-M3-POSTB1-HPRET") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

Normal notices never count: '60 days overdue, service suspends per contract', polite chasers, 'please prioritise', a reminder that a due date has passed. A vendor's claim that its own bank account is frozen, blocked or under review, offered with new payment details and a short deadline, IS the pattern.

If the basis is a TOTAL fee for the engagement: everything billed so far including this invoice (exact_facts.cumulative_billed is the structured figure; add paid priors if it is missing) exceeds it. If it is a fee PER PERIOD: this invoice's substantive lines together bill more than the fee for the period. If it is RATES or fixed milestone amounts: a line, or a milestone or period billed across several lines taken together, is billed higher than its stated rate or amount. If it is only a CAP: cumulative billing exceeds a cap that appears only in the prose; a cap that is also the PO's structured maximum or the contract's structured maximum is compared by code, and when the prose figure conflicts with the structured one the structured one governs, so NO. Billing at or below the basis is NO. If the text states no price for what is billed, NO. If the invoice currency differs from the currency of the stated basis, NO (no comparison is made).

question: At least one substantive line of this invoice is described so generically that its own text does not say what was bought, for which period, or under which authorization: "Professional services", "Consulting services", "Services rendered", "Work performed", "Project work per agreement", "Professional fees". Judge the line text itself, not what the PO or contract would let you guess. A line that names a deliverable, item, part or work code is specific even if brief; a period, quantity or rate alone does not rescue a line that never says what was bought. A code or abbreviation that any document in the packet decodes is specific; one nothing in the packet decodes is vague; a work-order, ticket or project code counts as specific only where the packet ties it to a described item, service or deliverable. Naming only the project or engagement the work relates to does not cure a line that never says what was bought. Tax, freight and expense lines do not count.

question: Invoice line 1 ("Tax compliance calendar — CFS Ltd.: Research federal and state filing requirements and draft annual compliance timeline for Cedarwell Financial Services Ltd.") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

question: The project owner or approver has declined invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") BY NAME in the packet: an approval comment, owner note or email saying this specific item was not commissioned, not requested, not authorised, or is excluded ("approved except for X", "we did not order the Y"); rejecting a named line because it was never authorised declines it, and so does an approval that accepts the invoice except this named line, whatever reason it gives. A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

question: Invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

Normal notices never count: '60 days overdue, service suspends per contract', polite chasers, 'please prioritise', a reminder that a due date has passed. A vendor's claim that its own bank account is frozen, blocked or under review, offered with new payment details and a short deadline, IS the pattern.

question: At least one substantive line of this invoice is described so generically that its own text does not say what was bought, for which period, or under which authorization: "Professional services", "Consulting services", "Services rendered", "Work performed", "Project work per agreement", "Professional fees". Judge the line text itself, not what the PO or contract would let you guess. A line that names a deliverable, item, part or work code is specific even if brief; a period, quantity or rate alone does not rescue a line that never says what was bought. A code or abbreviation that any document in the packet decodes is specific; one nothing in the packet decodes is vague; a work-order, ticket or project code counts as specific only where the packet ties it to a described item, service or deliverable. Naming only the project or engagement the work relates to does not cure a line that never says what was bought. Tax, freight and expense lines do not count.
